title: Toes-to-Bar — Individualized Mayhem Block
subtitle: 8-week technique-first toes-to-bar block
summary: Eight weekly sessions built from the uploaded Mayhem TTB/Core Endurance cycle. The source cycle trains high-rep toes-to-bar endurance and assumes the skill already exists; David's kipping attempts currently reach knees-to-elbows, so this lane first buys the missing piece — full toe contact and the return swing — and lets volume grow only as contact becomes ordinary. Every week shows the original Mayhem prescription as source context and a scaled session as the actionable default. Begin only after the 17–21 August FMD is finished and refeeding is complete, and weigh every session against what the week's WODs already took from grip, hanging and trunk.

primarySkill.title: The one skill this block trains
primarySkill.cue: Press the bar away with active lats, ride hollow-to-arch, drive the knees high while the hips close, then finish with a late knee-extension toe flick to the bar — and on the way down drive the feet down and push the bar away into the next arch.
primarySkill.failureSignal: When the active shoulder collapses, the return swing dies into a dead hang, or reps become knee lifts with no late flick, the set is over. A near contact is recorded as a near contact — never forced into a rep.

spacingNote: One toes-to-bar session a week, starting only after the 17–21 August FMD and a full refeed. Keep at least 48 hours between this session and the week's biggest pulling, hanging or GHD day — and when the WODs already delivered that volume, shrink or skip the session rather than stacking it.

warmup.title: Skill primer — before anything metabolic
items: 30–45 s active hang, lats pressing the bar down, shoulders away from the ears
2×5 controlled beat swings — hollow to arch, feet together
2×5 slow hanging knee raises — knees high, quiet lower, no borrowed swing
3–5 knees-high + late toe-flick singles, completely fresh — the best reps of the day

sessionRules.title: Rules for every session
items: The Mayhem numbers on each card are source context, not the day's target — the scaled lane is the session.
A full rep needs both feet on the bar together, inside the hands, with the shoulders still active. Anything else is a near contact — count it honestly and separately.
Skip or shrink the session when the week's WODs already carried roughly 30 or more pulling or hanging reps, or a big GHD dose, inside the previous 48 hours.
Stop the toes-to-bar portion when the return swing disappears, the shoulders go passive, or grip turns doubtful — then finish the core stimulus with V-ups, GHD sit-ups or toes-to-ring instead.
Substitutes keep the engine honest, but they never buy back failed technique — a session where the flick died early is logged that way and repeated.
No butterfly work and no chest-to-bar volume inside this block — chest-to-bar stays a separate low-volume technique exposure.

progressionRule: Advance to the next week only when the current week's contact target arrived with the return swing intact; repeat a week after a session where contacts or the return swing degraded. Progress is earned by contact quality, never by the calendar.

feedbackPrompt.title: Tell Nabu after each session

Shoulder and grip fatigue — none / noticeable / limiting

mustHave: The 17–21 August FMD is finished and refeeding is complete — this block never opens fasted or half-refed
Roughly six smooth strict knees-high reps near or at contact, as verified on 18 August
A secure grip setup — the fingerless gymnastics grips confirmed on 15 August

notes: General abdominal strength is not the limiter — contact mechanics and shoulder/grip endurance are, so the sessions spend their freshness there.
Technique guidance here is not medical advice — your floor coach overrides the app.

wodScaling.title: Reconcile with the week's WODs
wodScaling.intro: The source cycle assumes toes-to-bar endurance already exists. David's training week often already contains pulling, hanging, GHD and trunk volume — so the weekly dose bends around the WODs, never the other way round.
points: Count the week honestly: kipping pull-ups, toes-to-bar or knees-to-elbows inside WODs, strict pulling, rope work and GHD all draw from the same shoulder-and-grip account.
After a high-volume pulling or grip day, take at least 48 hours before this session — or run the primer only and bank the session for later in the week.

When a WOD programs toes-to-bar, scale it to small quality sets from rep one — knees-to-elbows with the late-flick attempt once contact fades — and tell the coach the block is acquiring contact, not capacity.
Never let a WOD's toes-to-bar volume plus this session's attempts exceed what one week of shoulders and grip can absorb — the session shrinks first.
Ordinary kipping pull-ups stay WOD maintenance during this block — no separate pull-up capacity work alongside it.

gates.title: Kept out of this block
gates.intro: Both have their own lane. Neither belongs inside these eight weeks.

items.requirement: Remains a separate, low-volume technique exposure — at most one short quality look per week when recovery allows, and never appended to a toes-to-bar session.
Stays deferred until ordinary kipping proficiency is substantially higher — roughly 15–20 clean unbroken kipping pull-ups — and is learned under a coach directly watching the shoulder path.

homeBarSubstitutions.title: Home bar — 80 cm wall clearance
homeBarSubstitutions.intro: The home bar's 80 cm wall clearance cannot host a full hollow-to-arch toes-to-bar swing under fatigue, so dynamic attempts stay on the gym rig. At home, train the pieces instead.
points: Strict hanging knee raises in small controlled sets — knees high, quiet lower, no swing.
Hollow rocks and V-ups on the floor for the trunk stimulus.
Active hangs and scap pull-ups for lat pressure and grip endurance, stopped before hot spots.
No kipping toes-to-bar attempts on this bar — a cramped swing rehearses the wrong return and is not technique volume.

m60Scaling.title: Masters (60+) scaling
m60Scaling.intro: Skill acquisition and workout scaling are different jobs. Keep them separate.
points: In skill work, run the scaled lane exactly — small fresh sets, never rushed reps under fatigue.
In metcons, substitute V-ups, hanging knee raises or moderate-depth GHD sit-ups for prescribed toes-to-bar volume rather than chasing Rx numbers.
Use the lower machine-calorie figure in every source workout, and slow the ski/row/bike pace before letting movement quality slip.
Never convert prescribed toes-to-bar 1:1 into maximal strict work; ask the floor coach when the intended stimulus is unclear.
During these eight weeks keep extra metcon hanging volume low, so the weekly session stays the best reps of the week.
